thread:
ryan: Quick question — Legal flagged a request to retain a specific SIEM export bundle for 7 years for an external audit. How do we reconcile that with our standard 365d retention + KMS-wrapped archival workflow? Need a safe, auditable unwrap flow and RBAC that doesn't create a permanent privileged role. @marta can you weigh in? :eyes:

marta: Short answer: do not grant a standing unwrap role. We should use timeboxed unwraps with a ticketed approval and ephemeral creds. Typical pattern: export -> archive-bucket (cmk) -> legal requests timeboxed unwrap -> approval workflow issues ephemeral service account that can call kms:Decrypt for that object only.

sam: Agree. A couple concrete notes: 1) Export objects must be labeled with retention_tag and audit_case_id. 2) Use an export-sub-bucket per audit where lifecycle is set to never-delete until case closes. 3) Access via temporary signed URLs + KMS-unlock recorded in audit log.

ryan: How do we keep the auditors from copying raw logs off the archive? They will insist on copies for their analysis. Need a documented enforcement + minimization approach.

marta: Two levers: access control + data minimization. For external auditors we can provide a pre-scrubbed dataset or a scoped read-only access via bastion that prevents download (or logs and alerts on large egress). If they absolutely must take a copy, require Legal + InfoSec signoff and record chain-of-custody ticket.

sam: Operational playbook sketch (one-liner steps):
1) Create an "audit-case" folder in archive-bucket with cmk tag.
2) Mark objects with metadata: audit_case=CASE-2026-123, retain_until=YYYY-MM-DD.
3) Open ticket T-XXXX for unwrap window (start/end).
4) Run ephemeral unwrap job scoped to that folder, with KMS condition binding for the object prefix.
5) Log the unwrap action to audit-trail collector and notify oncall.

ryan: Can you paste the minimal IAM condition example? Want to throw it into the ticket template.

sam: Sure — minimal IAM condition we use for ephemeral unwraps:```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01",
      "Condition": {
        "StringEquals": {"kms:EncryptionContext:archive_prefix": "audit/CASE-2026-123/"},
        "DateLessThan": {"aws:CurrentTime": "2027-03-01T00:00:00Z"}
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

marta: Also add an explicit requirement to rotate CMK after high-risk exposures and to require a second approver (Legal + SecOps) for any unwrap longer than 72h.

ryan: Sounds good. For SIEM exports pipeline: do we need a separate consumer key for exports vs internal queries?

sam: Yes. Exports should land in a hardened bucket with its own key and a strict ACL. Internal queries continue to use streaming/search indexes with short TTLs.

ryan: Who owns the ticket template update? I'll spin up TICKET-901 and draft the template, want SecOps + Legal signoff before we roll.

marta: I'll review the template and add the checklist for vulnerability triage scenarios (if export contains PII or secrets, require redaction or additional HSM wrapping).

auditbot: Note: when an unwrap event occurs, the pipeline will emit a webhook to #eng-security with event id and CMK id. Ensure runbook references event id for post-mortem correlation.

ryan: Great — will push draft this afternoon. Tagging @legal in the ticket. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
